question: Does access to a concrete prior search episode change allocation, duplicate rediscovery or valid yield, and is any apparent gain just retrieval of a known certificate?

inputs.source_episode_selection: Fixed primary v2 gpt-6.1-sol baseline replicate1 for each task, all3 recorded actions. No source selection by performance. Freeze byte hashes before calls.
inputs.packet: Exact source target, all action knob records and aggregate evaluation/validity/cost summaries, plus its retained best explicit certificate. No human-added target strategy.
inputs.source_outcomes: Exposed prior work, deliberately supplied as memory; not a held-out answer key.

conditions.name: same_target_episode
conditions.memory: Fixed completed source episode from the current target.

conditions.name: other_target_episode
conditions.memory: Same-format source episode from the other target, accurately labeled with its actual target.

primary_contrasts: W-U: relevance of an authentic recorded episode
W-C: warm-snapshot package versus cold start
U-C: unrelated but truthful prior episode versus cold start
metrics: search calls and realized candidate evaluations
duplicate schedules relative to all candidates in the frozen source episode
best cost strictly below the source episode incumbent
novelty_rule: Do not call a copied or rediscovered source certificate a new result. Compare each candidate schedule with the entire frozen source episode, not just visible files. This is source-relative index-schedule novelty, not global novelty or general DAG isomorphism.
analysis: Four task×replicate pairs per contrast; descriptive, unmatched model randomness. Packets are generated by a fixed extraction rule but can differ in length/content; record exact bytes/words/tokens. No autonomous retrieval, persistent-memory learning or model-weight change is claimed.
acceptance: Source episodes independently audited; exact packet/source hashes frozen; interface/source preflight before live calls; every resulting candidate and complete denominators checked independently.
